content:
Jimmy Kimmel Thursday night monologue featured an unexpected guest when his "assistant" Natalie burst into the studio and immediately clung to the host.

"This man is my guardian and protector," she said.

The reference was to President Donald Trump's aide Natalie Harp, who, according to The New York Times, had described Trump in a series of what were described as "reverent" letters as her "guardian and protector for this life."

When Kimmel told his "Natalie" to sit down, she sat on the floor at his feet. When he helped her up, she gushed: "Your hands are so smooth, your body is so strong."

The person playing Natalie appeared to be Kimmel's real-life wife Molly McNearney, who is also the show's executive producer and co-head writer. As she was dragged out of the studio, she shouted: "Your wife doesn't deserve you."

Trump is rarely seen without Harp by his side, a relationship so unusual that last month Georgia Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff was making national headlines just for briefly mentioning her at a rally.

Ossoff said: "She doesn't want this job, she wants to be at the disco and on Natalie flying around on the palace in the sky the emir of Qatar gave them." His remarks kicked off weeks of discussion about Trump and his aide.
